checks_performed.open_questions_resolvability:
FAIL. Applying this session's established standard (deferral is not acceptable when the design stage could reasonably resolve the question from material already reachable in the same session), three of the five open questions are resolvable now and should have been resolved by CODE-DESIGNER rather than pushed to ELIXIR-DEV:

(1) OQ-1b (whether :TasksComplete authorization requires the caller to be the task's current assignee, i.e. whether claim must precede complete for AC2's ops-approve/CEO-co-sign steps): the design states 'lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's policy table for :TasksComplete was not read in full this session'. It is a short, easily located file the design already needed to reason about (it already cites Engine.complete_task/3 and the router's authz_post macros). Reading it (this review did) shows evaluate_access/2's :AllowWithRowFilter branch applies ONLY to the :TasksList endpoint (`if endpoint == :TasksList and is_task_worker_only?(...)`); every other permitted endpoint, including :TasksComplete, gets `%AccessDecision{kind: :Allow, task_scope: :all}` -- there is no assignee-scoped row filter and no assignee check at all for :TasksComplete. Combined with the design's own already-confirmed fact that Engine.complete_task/3 does not check assignee as a precondition, this DEFINITIVELY resolves OQ-1b: claim is NOT required before complete under current code. The design should state this and specify each step as exactly one POST /complete call (matching the scenario's literal 3-step count), not leave it as an implementation-time decision.

(2) OQ-2 (the exact GET /api/v1/tasks query-param shape for resolving a just-created HUMAN_TASK's id by instance_id): lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex's handle_list/3 (already the file the design's own route table cites) directly answers this -- `parse_instance_id_param(Map.get(query, "instance_id"))` confirms `GET /api/v1/tasks?instance_id=<uuid>` is the real, already-implemented filter. This is not a deep-dive requiring speculative reverse-engineering; it is the same file's handler body, a few lines past what was already read to build the route table.

(3) OQ-3 (which literal string Engine writes as assignee_ref for a role:-attributed HUMAN_TASK node, needed to pick each actor's roles: list): lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex's resolve_assignee/1 (`{Map.get(attributes, "assignee_type"), Map.get(attributes, "role")}`) shows assignee_ref for a role-attributed node is exactly the literal `role` attribute string (e.g. "role-ceo" from process_route_approval.yaml's `role: role-ceo`), and tasks.ex's ROLE-scope query clause (`t.assignee_type == "ROLE" and t.assignee_ref in ^role_names`) confirms an actor's granted roles list must literally contain that same string to claim/complete the task. Both are short, directly-adjacent files to ones the design already cites (Engine, Tasks) -- this was reachable in the same session, not a genuinely unknowable fact.

OQ-1 (no distinct CEO actor in org_structure.yaml) is a closer call -- it is a fixture-content decision rather than a fact recoverable by reading more source -- but even there the design should have picked one option (reusing dept-mgmt's Alice is clearly the lower-risk, no-fixture-change default consistent with 'REQ-205's fixture is otherwise frozen') and recorded the choice, rather than leaving a coin-flip for ELIXIR-DEV to make silently. This is noted as a should-fix but is not, on its own, the basis for this FAIL -- OQ-1b/OQ-2/OQ-3 are.
